original_card.question: Can a specified pair of consecutive calls eliminate a restoration that the next call reconstructs?
methods: Write typed entry/exit contracts and a contracting multitype recurrence.
Derive a lower bound for the compulsory transitions of one proposed typed interface.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Show actual eliminated work and legal composition; changing a scalar recurrence into a matrix is insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Find a concrete consecutive-call boundary in the selected review and list its entry/exit obligations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Specify two call types and one operation actually removed by composition; derive the normalized recurrence.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Eliminating compulsory boundary work can lower recursive cost beyond packing gains.
allowed_variations: A two-type pilot or one explicit deferred restoration.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting the old scalar recurrence as a matrix without eliminating work.

actual_scope: Infinite-order two-coordinate shear drift carried through 53 fixed equivariant children, with all terminal powers lowered to paid ADD and doubling/halving instructions.
scope_change_reason: Finite-order cyclic and noncommuting finite-group boundaries are already covered. This tests an infinite-order drift; a sharp unit-power obstruction separates the new compressed-return tariff from free power assumptions.
bottleneck_link: A possible reduction in compulsory recursive boundary work. This is an abstract fixed-child interface pilot; no selected supplier is instantiated and no new kappa is inferred.
stop_rule: One k=53,m=5 fixture, one nested 3-by-17 tree, exponents -80..80, all ternary 2-by-4 readers, and 180 finite unit-tariff cases. Stop after exact endpoints, invoices, prefix growth and controls agree; no search for a global gate optimum.
evidence: README.md and RESULT.json, reproduced by verify.py through VERIFY.json.
author: Sagar Thakrar
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in derivation, implementation, independent arithmetic representation, verification and writing. One agent; no independent human review.
